RULES UNDER HIE LAND AND REVENUE REGULATION. 

OnATTEB L 

SETTLEMENT KITLES, 

SrC’TlON I. 

GENERAL PROVISIONS 

1. In these rales, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context— 

(а) Special cultivation meant, cultivation which involves, either ov'ing to the nature of 

the crop or owing to the process of cultivation, a much largci expenditure of Definationa. 
capita) per acre than is incurred by most of the cultivators m the province. 

Ordinary cultivation means onltivalion other than special cultivation. 

(б) Waste lAtid means land at the ibsposal of the Administration, which the Adrnmis* 
tration has not disposed of by lease, grant or otherwivc, and wtneh is not in- 
cluded in tt forest reserve, or in a jiroteuted forest constituted under the rules 
and has not been ailotod os a grazing ground under nile.| frauicd under section 
13 of the Assam Land and Revenue R^ulatinu, aa extended t.i Manqmr. 

(c) An annual lease means a lease granted for one year only and con fcih no tight in the 
soil beyond a right of user for the year for which it is given. It confers no 
right of transfer, or of iuhentanow beyond the year of issue, or of subletting. 

(d) A periodic lease, eidept, in tbe case of town land, meana a lease granted for a 
period longer than one year, and in tho case ol town land, a lease for a period 
longer than three years. Subject to and so far as is oonsistenf with any restric- 
tions, conditions and limitations contained therein, it conveys to the ierse the 
rights of a iand>|io]rlcr as defined in tho Assam Land and Revenue Regulation, 
as extended to Manipur.

Rules under Section 544 of the Code of Criminal Procedure regulating the payment of Government 
Servants summoned by the Criminal Courts in the Stato of West Bengal & the Union Territory 
>of Manipur to give evidence in their Oifioial capacity. 


t'nder the provisions of Section 644 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Act V of 1808) resd 
yith the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs Notification No. F 2/1/57-Judl.lf dated 
^e 3rd Juno, 1957 and in pursuanoo of reciprocal arrangoments entered into hy ilio Governraeni 

India with the Government of West Bengal, the Chief Commidjiioud; . Manipuj- been pleased 
J(k> prescribe tho following rules for regulating the payment of expenses of Government Servants 
sjiummoned by Criminal Courts in the States of West Bengal & the Xfuion Territory of Manipur 
^to give evidenoe in their official capacity, namely : — 

1. In criminal eases to which tlie State is a party, a Government servant giving evidenoe 

regarding facts of which he has official knowledge will, on production of the certificate of atten< 

dance issued by the summoning court, be paid travelling aliowaooe by the Government under 
whom he is serving. 

2. In criminul cases to which the State is not a party, a Govern meat servant giving evidenoe 

sipigarding facts of which he has official knowledge will be paid travelling allowance by the sum- 

moning court according to the rules under which such Government servant draws his travelling 
allowanoe for a jaurney on tour, and the charges will be borne by the Union Territory of Manipur 
or the Government of West Bengal according as the court is situated in the Union Territory of 
Manipur or in the State of West Bengal. 

3. When a Government Servant serving in a Commercial Department, or when any other 

officer is summoned to give evidenoe as a technical or expert witness the pay of the €lovernment 

servant concerned for the period of his absence from his headquarters and travelling allowanoe 
and other expenses due to him will first bo borne by the Government under whom he is serving 
and subsequently be recovered from the Union Territory of Manipur or the Government of West 

Bengal according as the Court in which the officer is summoned to give evidenoe is situated 

in the Union Territory of Manipur or the State of West Bengal.

No. l6/3S/59-SC/S(D)--ln order to encourage the art of Wood-(\'irving, Drawing and Painting 
i^moDg the tribal people of Manipur it ia decided to organise a competition on all Manipur level 
and prizee will be awarded to the beat candidates. The following rules have been framed for 
the said competition and all those who are interested are requoatfd to participate in the said 
•ompetition. The last date to participate to tbs competition is Slat December, 1959. 

RULES FOR WOOD CARVING : DRAWING AND PAINTING COMPETITION. 

Wood Carving : 

(1) It is open to all tribals in Manipur irroapootive of ago. 

(2) The carvings may be of any subject and of any size say animals, human figures, 

images and so on. ihey may be painted or not according to the desire of the 
competitor. 

(3) The carvings should normally be done ia the local stylo and be in line with the 
traditional products of the area. 

(4) The carvings should bo specially for this competition and the competitors must 

be willing to sell them if market can be found for them. The name of the 

competitor or the price should not be carved or written or pasted on the car- 

vings. It will be sufficient if a brief description is givcm for identification in a 
covering letter or there could bo a label securely tied but not pasted on tbcj 
article. 

(6) Three prizes would bo given, the first prize carrying a sum of Rs. 100/-, the 
second prize Bs. 50/- and the third Hs. 25/-. 

Drawing & Painting : 

(6) Prizes of Ils. 100 Rs. 50/- and Rs. 25/- will be awarded for the best drawing 
and painting produced by tribals living in Manipur. 

( 7 ) The competition is open to all tribal boys and girls under 20 years of ago, 

(8) The medium used can be either pen or pencil, crayon or paint and brush and 
the drawings or paintings should be on either double or single sheets of foolscap 
paper. 

(0) The artists should illustrate any of the following according to their own ideas. 

(a) Agriculture. 

(b) Rt ligion. 

(c) Daneing. 

(d) Cottage Indpstries. 

(10) All people in the picture should be drawn in their own dress and where buil« 
dings are shown, they should bo in the local style of architecture. As a back* 
ground, the local scenery bills, forests or rivers can be included. 

(11) No rulers or compasses should be used, 

Cmunon Rules to Both Competition : 

(12) There will be no entrance fees for these competitions* 

(13) The competition will be at one level i. o. All Manipur level. 

(14) The last date for submission of the articles is 31st December each year. 

(15) Tilt) articles should be sent to the Deputy Commissioner (Tribal Welfare) through 
the Sub-Divisional Officers/ Sub-Deputy OoUcetors oonoerned or direct on or before 
this date. The prizes will be awarded during the Republic Day (Celebrations at 
suoh places as may be notified later.

Subject : — Republic Day Celebrations 1960 — Presentation of Tableaux by the 
Manipur Administration. 

Applications with designs are invited from Tableaux Designers of Manipur for a Tableaux to 
b© presented by the Manipur Administration in the Cultural Pageant on the forthcoming Republic 
Day Parade at New Delhi. The themes should be sociologioal and cultural rather than agricultural 
or industrial. Themes ef the latter type can also be considered provided they result in tableaux 
of outstanding excellence and appeal and have special signitioanoe against the events of the day. 
The applieations should reach the Publicity Officer by the 31st August, 1959 along with the 
writes-up and sketches which should be illustrated by colour drawings large enough to give an 
idea of what the actual tableaux will look like. A prize value not more than Rs. 150/- will 
be awarded to the best designer provided the design is accepted for production and (jonsolation 
prizes of Rs. 60/- and Rs. 25/* may also be awarded to the 2ad and 3rd designers respectively. 
Designs similar to those accepted in previous years need not be Bubmitted. The design sliuuld 
b© capable of and suitable for production at the Parade. The Folk Danoo and Tableaux Committee 
formed for the purpose will select throe tableaux out of them and recommend to the Ministry 
of Defence^ New Delhi for final selection.

Subject F01.K DANCES ON THE OCCASION OP THE REPUBLIC DAY 
CELEBRATION AT NEW DELHI, 1960 -SELECTION OF TEAMS 
FOR MANIPUR. 

Applications arc invited from the local teams or organisations in Manipur who desire to participate 
in the Folk Dance Celebrations at New Delhi in January, 1960 on tlie occasion of the Republic 
Day Celebrations, through the Local Committees so as to reach the undersigned on or before 
Slst August, 1950 during office hours. They will be required to stage dance shows at 7.00 P.M. 
at the Manipuri Dance College Hall on the 10th September, 1959 before the Central Folk Pances 
and Tableaux Selection Committee which will be formed for this purpose. The Committee will 
select three teams from Hill areas two from the valley for the folk dance for recommendation 
to the Ministry of Defence, xNew Delhi for final selection. 

2. Preliminary selection of dance teams from the Sub-divisions will be done by the Sub- 
Divisional Officers concerned with the help of a local committee constituted by them for this 
purpose at a local competition held at thoir Head Quarters. Two teams of folk dances — one 
tableaux if possible, will bo selected by each Sub- Divisional Officer. For the Sadar area including 
Imphal proper and for areas where there is no Sub-Divisional Officer the Deputy Commissioner 
will hold a competition at Imphal along the same lines as the Sub-Divisional Officers in th© 
Sub Divisions. If any of the tribal teams from neighbouring hill area find it more convenient 
to j(]>pear before the Deputy Commissioner’s Committee at Imphal it may do so. The Deputy 
Comnnsbioner will select three teams from the valley and two teams from the hill areas from 
those v/ho appear before him. Such selected teams will have to join in the oompetitiou stated in 
para I above. Detail writes-up and photos o? each dance item should be sent by the Sub- 
Diviciiunal Officers and the Deputy Commissioner to the Assistant Secretary (P), Manipur Administration 
hy Slst August, 1959 positively. The selection at the level of the Sub Divisional Officer and the 
Deputy Commissioner should therefore be finished on or before the 26th August, 1969.

RESOLUTION 

No, SSl(A)-28(43)/S8. — The Government of India in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
have been considering the establishment of an agency for giving encouragement to small artisans, 
and ieohnioians with inventive skill to work out details and specifications of processes, appliances 
and gadgets by giving awards and financial and technical assistance to persons whope inventions 
in the sphere of small industries are of a distinctive character and of marked value in the 
development and commercial exploitation of small industries. In order to give inducement in this 
direction, it has been decided to sot up a Small luventi ms Development Board at the Headquar- 
ters in the Office of the Development Commissioner for Small Scale Industries and with State 
Boards in each of the States, The Government will, from time to time, place at the disposal 
of the ]’>evelopmeut Committisioner suitable funds for distribution as awards and for fiuanoial and 
technical assistance. 

2. The oomporition and functions of the Central and State Boards will be as follows 

(a) Regional Boards, — They would consist of the Director of the Small Industries Service 
Institute in the State ; the Directors of Industries of tiie State ; two other technical experts and 
one technical officer of the State Government concerned. 

The inventors will bring to the notice of the State Board their inventions for the purpose of 
aeeuring awards and financial assistance. The State Board will m>ike an initial teohnioal scrutiny 
of the details of the processes or gadgets or inventions and of its usefulness. If found deserving 
of support on account of its utility, the State Boards will recommend such inventions for finan* 
•ial assistance, technical assistance and/or awards to the Central Board. 

(b) GuBtral Board* — The Central Board will be named ''The Board for Promotion of Small 
Inventions’' and will consist of the following members : — 

(1) Shri M.S. Thacker, Secretary, Ministry of Soioniifio Research and Cultm^I Affaim. ChairmM* 

(2) Shri Nagendra Bahadur, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Commerce and Xnduetry. 

(3) Dr. B.D. Kalelkar, Senior Industrial Adviser (Engineering), Development Wing. 

(4) Dr. Lai C. Verman. Director, Indian Standards Institution, New Delhi* 

(5) Shri M.N. Dastur, Managing Director, M/S. Dastur and Co. (P) Ltd, ^17 Miseitn Row; 
Calcutta. 

(6) Shri T.R. Gupta, M/S. Jay Engineering Works Ltd., 183^ Prince Anwar, Shah Roadf 
Calcutta — 31. 

(7) ^hri P,B, Bhina Krishnan, M,P.. 17, Canning Lane, New Delhi~l.

ae Convener of the Board. 

The reooinmendations received from the State Board will be oonsiderod and examined by the 
Central Board for finally recommending the grant of awards. 

3. The Central Board will frame snitalde rules in regard to the liuanoial and teohnioal assis- 
tance and the number of awards to bo given, the conditions subject to which they will be eano- 
tioned and the amounts of different awards. The Board will from time to time gi’re publicity

allowance by the summoning court according to the rules under which such Govtru* 
inent servant draws his travelling allow^ance for a journey on lour, and Ihe charges

RULES UNDER THE POISONS ACT, 1919. 

1. la thowse Rules, the “Act” means, the Poisons Act, 1919. 

2. (1) The substanoes ineiitipned in the Schedule hereto annexed shall bo deemed to be poi- 
sons for the purposes of these rules. 

(2) Except in the case of white, yellow, red, brown and black arsenic, these rules shall 
apply only to the . pos^sessiioa for sale, and the sale of specifted poisons within th# 
limits of municipalities and , cantonments. 

3. Unless exempted under the^. provisions of :^^he Act, no person sh^ll sell or . possess for sale 
,any poison specihed in rule 2 exj^ept under a licence granted by th^ .District Magistrate, or tb^ 
Sub-Divisional Magistrate or any Magistrate specially empowered by the District Magistrate within 
their respective jurisdictions. 

4. The grant, withdrawal, cancellation or revocation of a licence to any applicant shall be 

, at the discretion of the issuing aujthority subject ^ to appeal to the District Magistrate ,or the 

, Chief Commissioner as the case may be, if issued, withdrawn, oanoelled or revoked by an officer 
immediately subordinate. 

5. Subject to the . provisions of Rules 6 and 7— a licence granted under Rule 3 shall remain 

in force for one year from the Ipt January or the date of issue, if later than the 1st January, 

to the Slat December following. Every applicant for the grant or renewal of a licence shall make 
a written application to the issuing authority. 

N> 

6. A lioentie shall terminate on the death of the lioence-holder, or if granted to a Firm or 
Company, on the winding np or transfer of the business of such Firm or Company. Provided 

^ that if the Firm or Company is transferred as a gcing concern to any new party, and the trans. 
feree applies for a fresh licence within fourteen days of the date of transfer, the subsisting licence 
ahall continue in force until a new licence has been granted or refused by the issuing authority, 

or until the date of expiry under Rule 6 whichever is earlier.

9. A licenoe.holder shall not soli any poison to any person unless the latter is personally 
known to him, or ideiuified to bis satisfaction. Ho shall nut sell any poison to any person who 
appears to him to be under the age of 18 or any person who does not appear to him to be in 
full possession of his faculties, or to any wandering madicant. 


10. (i) Evwy licence- holder shall maintain a regi'^ter in wdiich he shall enter all sates of poison 

other than those used by a chemist, druggist or compounder diapending or compounding in comf^Ii- 
anoe with the proscription of a medical or veterinary practitioner. The following particulars shall 
be entered in such register in respect of each sale namely : — 


(a) Name of poison 

(b) Quantity sold 

(c) Date of sale 

(d) Name and address of purchaser 

(e) Purpose for which the poison was stated by the purchaser to be required* 

(f) Signature «)f purchaser (or thumb impression il illiterate) or in case of purchase by pOnSt, 
date of letter or written order and referdneo to the original in the file in which 
it is preserved. 

(g) Signature of vendor. 

(ii) In a separate portion of the registration shall be entered, in separatee columns for oaoh 
poison, the quantity of each sold daily, and these entries shall be filled up from day to day. 

(iii) The signature under item (g) of the register shall be that of the lioenoe-holder himself, 
or when the lioenoe-hclder is a Firm or Company, that of an accredited representative of such 
Firm or Company, and shall be entered at the time of sale or despatched to the purchaser. 
Such signature shall be held to imply that the writer has satsfied himself that the reijuirements 
of Buie 9 have been fulfilled. 


(iv) All latters or written orders referred to in head (f) of the register shall be preserved 
in origmal by the licence- holder for a period of not less than two years from the date cl 
sale. 


11. (i) A licence-holder shall maintain in respect of each poison specified in Bole 2— a stock 

register which shall contain the following particulars : 

(a) Serial Number 

(b) Dale 

(c) Amount received 

(d) Name and address of person from whom received 

(e) Amount sold 

(f) Balance in stock 

(g) Remarks 

(11) The Stock Register shall be totalled and balanced daily and the Lioenoe thall be himw’f 
Ie^.ponftible for its oorrectnesK. . , 

12. Any Magistrate or Police Officer of or aboFe the rank of Sab-Iliepeetor, W 

Inspootor or Sub-Inspector or any Medical Officer or above the rank of the Hoepltol A«.i8ta»l^ 
may at any tioi) visit and inspect the premises of a lioenoo-holder where poi«oa i« kept lox

13. All poinojis kept for salo by any lioence-bolder under these rules (except those kept by 

chemist, dru*^pis^ or compounder Tor the purpose of dispensing or compounding in complianoo 

with the proscription of a morlical (>r veterinary practitioner) shall be kept in a box, almirah, 

room or building (acoor 'ing to the quantity maintained) which shall be secured by lock and key 
and in which no substance shall be placed other than poisons possessed in accordance with a 
licence granted under tlie Act ; and each poison shall be kept, within such box, almirah, room 

or building in a separate closed recoptablo of glass metal or earthenware. Every such box, almirah, 
room or building and every such receptable shall be marked with the word ‘POISON* in red 
obaraoters both I jiglish and Vernacular, and in the case of recsptables containing separate poisons 
with the name of such poison. 

14. When any poi»ou is sold, it. shall be securely packed in a olo.sod receptacle or paoket 

{according to tlio quantity) and every such receptacle or packet shall be labelled by the vendor 
with a red label, bearing the name of the person in English and the vernacular and the number 
And date of the entry, in the register of sales specified in Rule 10. 

16, A licence-holder shall not sell powdered white arsenic to any person unless the same is, 

before the sale thereof, mixed with soot, indigo or Prussian blue, in the proportion of half an 
ounce of soot, indigo or Prussian blue at least to one pound of the white arsenic and so in 
proportion for any greater or leas quantity. 

Provided that there the Licensing Authority is satisfied that such arsenic is required for some 
purpose for which such admixture would according to the representation of the purchaser, render 
it unfit, the said Licensing Authority may authorise the vendor in writing to sell without such 
Admixture, such quantity of white arsenic as the Licensing Authority may think proper. 

16. Petrol containing ethyl fluid (as admixture of betra-ethyl lead) is exempted from the 

provisions of the Act and these rules provided — 

(i) the cans and pumps containing the duel are labelled to indicate the presence of tetra 
ethyl lead in the duel and to warn the user to avoid spillage and not to use the 
duel for purposes other than as motor duel ; 

(ii) the duel is dyed as an additional check against its use otherwise than as a motor 

duel : and 

(iii) the amount of lead tetra ethyl in the duel does not exceed 1 part in 1,300 part* 

by volume or 1 in 650 by weight. 

17. (i) No dealer shall send by post any poison in compliaoe with an order received by 

post or telegraph or any other means unless he is satiafiod that the order comes from or in 
Accordance with a prescription of a registered medical practitioner, or that it comes from a dealer, 

the head of a Government Department or a recognized school or College, or a research or 

medical institution or hospital or a charitable dispensary in charge of tjualified medical practitioner, 
or a recognized public body or undertrial firm. The sender of the order shall give such clear 
And necessary particulars about himself, his address and his business as will enable the dealer 
4o verify the bonafides of the sender, 

(ii) Any poison intended for , despatch by post shall bo securely package, distinctly marked 
**P0I80N** in red letters on the outer cover and duly registered. 

18. (i) The fee for each licence shall be Rs. 2/-. 

(ii) The fee for duplicate licence when the original is accidentally lost or destroyed and 

the fee for charge of the place of business shall be Re. 1/- in either case. 

(iii) All fees under these rules shall be paid in non-judioial stamp. 

19. All applications for renewal of licences shall be made one month prior to the date of 
oxpiiy. The fee shall be as prescribed in rule 17(1). If applications for renewal are not 

Asade before one month of the date of expiry, an additional fee of one rupee shall be charged*

Whereas, I am of opinion as the result of an enquiry held into the constitution, working^ 
endA&juoial condition of the Waiihou phumnom Mapal Fishing Co-operative Society Lid. R. No. 
that the society ought to be dissolved.

Imphal, the 30th October, 1959. 

The Government of India, Minutry of Scientific Research and Cultural Affairs, propose to bring 
out a Directory of Cultural Organisations in India. The Government of India therefore desires to 
have informations of all cultural Organisations in Manipur on the basis of the following points. 

(a) Name and address of the Organisation. 

(b) Objectives. 

(o) Date of Foundation. 

(d) Short Statements of activities. 

(e) Administered by whom (Name of present director). 

(f) Remarks. 

2. In order to enable this Administration to furnish the above information to the Govern- 
ment of India, all cultural Institution* iu Manii'ur are requested to furnish the informations to 
the Secretary (D) Manipur Administration on or before the 15th November, 1959.

THE SUGAR (SPECIAL EXCISE DUTY) ORDINANCE, 

1959. 

NO. 3 OF 1959. 

Promulgated by the President in the Tenth Year of the Rtpublic of India, 

An Ordinance to provide for the imposition of a special duty of excise 
on oertain sugar. 

Whereas ParliaineDt is not in aession and the President is satialied that 
circumstances exist wliioh render it necessary for him to take immediate action. 

Now, THEftEFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (1) of 
articles 123 of the Constitution, the President is pleased to promulgate the 
following Ordinance : — 

L (i) This Ordinance may be called the Sugar (Special Excise Duty) ^ido^^and 

Ordinance, 1969. comaienot.. 

i* , cieut 

(2) It shall come mto force at once. 

2. In this Ordinance, unless the context otherwise ro<iuires Dehiiiiiani. 

(а) “Central Exoises Aot" means the Ceutral Excises nnd Salt Act, 1944. 

(б) "factory” means any premises, including the precincts thereof, wherein 
or in any part of whioh sugar is being manufactured, or, wherein or in 
any part of whiol>, any manufacturing process connected with the production of 
sugar is being oarrjied on or is ordinarily carried on, and includes any pre- 
mises wherein sugar in respect of whioh the duty of excise payable under 
the Central Exoises Act or the Additional Duties of Excise (Uoods of Special 

.SB ■of 1957 

■ Importance) Aot, 1967, has not bten paid, is stored : 

(c) ‘‘sugar” means any form of sugar, whether wholly or partially manufactured, 
but does not include— 

(i) khandsari sugar, that is to say sugar in the manufacture of whioh 

neither a vacuum pan nor a vacuum evaporator is employed : or 

(ii) palmyra sugar, that is to say sugar manufactured from jaggery 

obtained by boiling the juioo of the palmyra palm. 

3. (I) There shall he levied and collected in respect of that quantity of 
sugar removed from any faotory on or after the commencement of this Ordi- 
nanoe as is equivalent to the quantity of sugar lying in stock on such oommenoa- 
meat within the prooinots of the factory, a special duty of exoiso at the rata 
•f rupees two and fifty-two naye paise psr owt. 

(2) The duty of excise referred to in sub-section { 1 ) shall be in addition 
to the duties of excise chargeable on sugar under the Central Excises Aot or 
any other low for the time being in force. 

(3) The provisions of the Central Exoises Aot and the rules thereunder, 
jniyiiTdfng those relating to refunds and exemptions from duty shall, so far as 
msy he, appfy in relation to the levy and collectbn of the special duty of 
soctiae reficred to in Buhaeotion (I) as they apply in relation to the levy 
and ooUeotiep of tiio duties of oxojse on sugar under the Central Ezsiass Aot.

OFFICE OF’ THE DIRECTOR OF INDUSTRIES MANIPUR 

PRESS NOTE 

Whites giTing financial Aid to Small Scale and Cottage Industries in this Territory 
under the existing State Aid to Industries Act ( Centrally Administered Areas ) Model Bute 
No. 1949, the Administration has decided the following guiding principles in regard to th« 
disposal of Industrial loan applications : — 

(1) The common place industries and processing industries such as rice mills, oil mills, loan* 
dries etc. are outside the scope of Small Scale Industrial loan under State Aid ta Indnstties. 

(2) The aid will be given to such industries which produce essential consumer goods and other 
articles or ancUlarary parts to feed larger industries that are in short supply in this part of tha 
country and hare to be either exported from outside or transported from long distances at con- 
siderable cost and wfaioh re<j[uire special aid and encouragement for their organisation or development. 

(3) Loan towards working capital will be given for starting deserving industries or well enited 
extension of deserting existing industries. 

(4) All deserving cottage and Village Industries intended to attain self sufficiency and self 
reliance in pupulagee and intended to serve the essential needs of rural population will bowevur 
be given State Aid. 

Applications for State Aid which do not fall under the above categories are liable to be rejected. 

B. MaNOHANDA 

Director of Industries Muiipnr.

OFFICE OF THE ACCOUNTANT GENERAL, ASSAM 
NOTIFICATION 

Shillong, the 9th November, 1969. 

No. TM 10/56/18 . — Attention of all Treasury and Sub'Treasnry Officers and all Gazetted Officers 
in Assam, Tripura and Manipur, N.E F.A. & N.H T.A. is invited to Section 18(2) of the Indian 
Income Tax Act, 1922. In accordance with the provision the Treasury and Sub-Treasury Officers 
shall at the time of payment of G. O’s pay and allowances deduct income tax and super tax on 

the amount payable at the rate representing the average of the rates applicable to the estimated 

total income of the assessee under “lalaries. ’ 

In order to enable the Treasury and Sub-Treasury officers to discharge this function. Gazetted ’ 
Offieers should furnish two statements one attached to the pay bills for March paid in April 
every year showing their estimated income for the ensuing year i. e. March to February, and the tax 
payable on the basis of such income and the average rate of deductions ; and the other attached 
to the pay bill of February payable in March every year showing actual income during the year* 
income tax payable on such income, the amounts paid during the preceeding months and the 
balaaoe payable. 

The Tieasury and Sub-Treasury Officers will not pass the bills unless the Statemente are attached. 

T. 0. KuiSRltAK, 

Deputy Accountant General, (Admn.)

It ia hereby uotified for genero] information that the exclusive right to work out timbers from 
the following Manipur Blocks indicated below will be sold by public auction at Jirimukh Range 
Office at 10-30 A. M. on the 28th December, 1959 on the following oonditions. 

2. The period of eontraot is 3 (three) years commencing from the date of acceptance of the 
•ale by Manipur Administration that may be iroin let January, 1960 uptu the 31t>t December, 196J. 

8. ITie sale will be on the basis of rate of Monopoly feo which bidders are prepared to offer 
over and above royalty in term of Naya Paise per Rupee of royalty payable on the extracted, 
timbers. The Monopoly fee offrred and accepted by Manipur Administration .shall be payable along 
with the Boyhlty and Sale-Tax at the Revenue Collection Station. 

4. No revision in the rates of royalty in res[>eot of the Blocks that can be worked only from the 
Jiribam side will be made before the expiry of their respeotive lease period or nutii such time that tho 
New Cachar Road is motorahle whichever is earlier. 

5. In case, the Monopoly fee offered by the bidders is considered inadequate, the Block may either 
be retained for resale or kept it unsold. 

6. The Manipur Administration reserves tho right to accept or reject any bid without assigning any 
veaeon therefor. 

7. The Manipur Administration does not take any responsibility for tho quantity and quality 
of timber that ma^ bo available lor removal from the said Blocks. Tho intending purchasers are 
advised to inspect the Blocks, 'fhey may approach tJio Forest Department for such help aemay 
be necessary in this respect. 

8. The »« ini"mnTi and maximum annual quota of logs to bo extracted is limited to 400 to 
700 logs respectively. No trees below 6 ft. in girth measured at breast height (i. e. 4^ ft. from 
ground) will be allowed to be out. 

9. Only those persons who have deposited a sum of Rs. 500.00 (Rupees live hundred i only 
for each Block in the Silchar or Iraphal Treasury as Earnest Money will be eligible for bidding 
at the auction. They should also produce beforehand the Inoome-Tax/Sale-Tax Clearance Certifleatee 
as also testimonials from the Forest Department showing 6 years’ experience in umber working. 
The intending bidders should apply to the Chief Forest Officer, Manipur euclosiug the Treasury 
Cholan, Sale-Tax and Income-Tax Clearance Certificates by the 23fd December, 1959 for registra- 
tion of their names as bidders* in the Auction. Failure to comply with the above mentioned oon- 
dltioDB will render a person ineligible, for biddin' at the auction. The Earnest Money will ba 
xefunded in case of unsaocessful bidders and will be eonverted to a part of caution money in 
ease of successful bidders. 

Provided, however, that if the euooeesful bidders whose bid has been acoepted, refuses or fails 
to sign the bid list and the agreement hereinafter menlioned, the said earnest money may be 
liable to be forfeited to the Government. 

10. 'Ihe Chief Forest Officer, Manipur may at his discretion disallow any person about whose 
f^mtation he is not satisfied to bid at the Auction. No bidder should be allowed to mgege or
